traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Phytolaccaceae, which takes in Lophiocarpaceae: leaves alternate; leaves simple; margins entire; veins pinnate; stipules usually absent, rarely present; plants usually hermaphrodite, sometimes dioecious; ovary superior; floral cup absent; stems usually herbaceous, sometimes woody; flowers solitary, in cymes, in racemes, in spikes or in panicles; flowers actinomorphic; perianth tepals; fruit capsule, berry, samara, nut, aggregate, schizocarp or drupe; stamens 4 to 50; carpels (1-) 4 to 12 (-16). Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.
